learning_outcomes.text: Adequately present and document the resolution of a problem, work, or project related to telecommunication systems.
Understand and use the fundamentals of programming in telecommunication networks and services.
Select the most appropriate transport layer protocol for a given application.
Describe, program, validate, and optimize communication protocols and interfaces.
Design and program telematics, network, and distributed services and applications.
Select and apply development technologies for distributed applications, mobile applications, and interactive applications.
Use computer tools for searching bibliographic resources or information related to network and telecommunication service programming tools.
Effectively communicate (in expression and comprehension), orally and in writing, the characteristics of the designed communication services.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to telematics applications on mobile devices and service integration
assessment_rules: For the ordinary examination, the theoretical block (TE) accounts for 60% and the practical block (PL) for 40%. A minimum score of 5.0 out of 10 is required for both the theoretical and practical blocks individually. The theoretical block score is the geometric mean of C1' (C1 + voluntary theoretical work up to 1 point) and C2. The practical block score PL is calculated as (0.65 * ExPL + 0.25 * EntPL) * (Mem / 10) + 0.10 * Mem, where ExPL is the geometric mean of E1 and E2, and EntPL is the geometric mean of practice submissions. If minimums are not met, the final grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4. In the extraordinary examination, the practical part and final report grade from the ordinary examination are retained, and a single written theoretical/practical exam is conducted, with the same 60/40 weighting.
